sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances, individual unit file
Colorado Secretary of State TRACER: contributions to Pueblo County candidates since 2023
EFF Atlas of Surveillance (police surveillance technology, searched by department)

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($45,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts itemized cash contributions from businesses, unions and political committees to Pueblo County candidates whose committee names a county office, reported to the Secretary of State's TRACER since 2023. Committees whose names do not show the office are left out, so this is a floor. Individuals, LLC members, in-kind gifts and party and candidate committees are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-14. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Colorado yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Pueblo County Sheriff's Office operates eight drones as of 2018, according to data compiled by the Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS003738, citing Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College

redFlags.label: Real-time crime center
redFlags.detail: The Pueblo Police Department launched a real-time crime center in 2024.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS013976, citing KOAA

redFlags.label: Gunshot detection (ShotSpotter)
redFlags.detail: The Pueblo Police Department installed Shotspotter over three square miles in 2023.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS013277, citing SoundThinking

redFlags.label: Third-party investigative platform
redFlags.detail: The Pueblo Police Department received an enterprise license for LexisNexis' Accurint Virtual Crime Center through its membership in the Colorado Information Sharing Consortium.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS012777, citing Government information

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: The Pueblo Police Department began using ELSAG automated license plate readers in 2010. PPD added another ALPR system in 2018. The Pueblo Transportation Department also added Nupark ALPR systems, which is checked against the Pueblo Police Department's hot lists.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS000044, citing City of Pueblo Colorado
